description: Computing with real numbers when exact answers are out of reach: errors, root finding, linear systems, eigenvalues, interpolation, integration and differential equations, each implemented and tested for accuracy and stability. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory numerical analysis course.
modelledOn: Chapra and Canale, Numerical Methods for Engineers
Heath, Scientific Computing: An Introductory Survey
outcomes: Explain floating-point representation and analyse round-off, truncation and propagated error and conditioning.
Find roots of nonlinear equations with bisection, fixed-point, Newton and secant methods and compare their convergence.
Solve linear systems with direct and iterative methods and understand pivoting, stability and condition numbers.
Approximate eigenvalues with the power method and QR iteration.
Construct interpolating polynomials and splines and fit curves by least squares.
Compute derivatives and integrals numerically and solve initial value problems with Euler and Runge-Kutta methods, with error control.

units.title: Error analysis and floating point
topics: Sources of error: modelling, measurement, truncation, round-off
IEEE 754 floating point: mantissa, exponent, machine epsilon, overflow, underflow, NaN
Absolute and relative error; significant digits; loss of significance and cancellation
Propagation of error; conditioning and stability of algorithms
Taylor series as the basis of numerical methods; order of convergence and big-O
Setting up Python with NumPy, or MATLAB, and writing reusable numerical routines

units.title: Nonlinear equations in one variable
topics: Bisection: bracketing, error bound, number of iterations
Fixed-point iteration and the contraction condition
Newton's method: derivation, quadratic convergence, failure cases, multiple roots
Secant and false-position methods; Muller's method in brief
Roots of polynomials: Horner's scheme, deflation; stopping criteria and convergence acceleration (Aitken)
Applications: break-even and interest-rate calculations, projectile range

units.title: Direct methods for linear systems
topics: Gaussian elimination with partial and scaled pivoting; operation counts
LU, Cholesky and LDL decompositions; solving multiple right-hand sides
Matrix norms, condition number and error bounds; ill-conditioned systems (Hilbert matrix)
Tridiagonal and banded systems; Thomas algorithm
Linear least squares via normal equations and QR

units.title: Iterative methods and eigenvalue approximation
topics: Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel and SOR; convergence conditions and diagonal dominance
Conjugate gradient in brief for large sparse systems
Power method and inverse power method for dominant and smallest eigenvalues; Rayleigh quotient
QR algorithm for all eigenvalues; Gershgorin circles
Applications: PageRank, vibration modes, principal components

units.title: Interpolation, curve fitting and polynomial approximation
topics: Lagrange and Newton divided-difference interpolation; error term; Runge's phenomenon
Hermite interpolation; Chebyshev nodes
Piecewise interpolation and cubic splines (natural and clamped)
Least-squares curve fitting: linear, polynomial and linearised exponential models
Orthogonal polynomials and approximation; Bezier curves for graphics
Fitting rainfall or sales data and judging the fit

units.title: Numerical differentiation and integration
topics: Forward, backward and central difference formulas; error and step-size trade-off; Richardson extrapolation
Newton-Cotes rules: trapezoidal, Simpson's, higher order; composite rules and error bounds
Romberg integration; adaptive quadrature
Gaussian quadrature; improper and multiple integrals
Applications: area under measured curves, work and energy, probability from densities

units.title: Initial value problems and ODEs
topics: Existence and well-posedness; Euler's method and its global error
Taylor methods; Runge-Kutta methods including classical RK4; adaptive step size (RK45)
Multistep methods: Adams-Bashforth and Adams-Moulton; predictor-corrector
Systems of ODEs and higher-order equations; stiffness and implicit methods
Stability regions; choosing a method
Project: simulate an epidemic (SIR), a pendulum or a circuit and validate against known solutions

schedule.title: Errors and floating-point arithmetic
schedule.exercise: Explain with one example why adding 0.1 ten times does not give exactly 1 in floating point arithmetic.

tasks.title: Classify the error in six given computations as modelling, measurement, truncation or round-off, and compute the size of each where data are given
Compute machine epsilon by halving a number in a loop, print the result for single and double precision and compare with the IEEE 754 value
Show catastrophic cancellation in the quadratic formula for roots of very different size, then rewrite it stably and compare relative errors

schedule.title: Conditioning, Taylor series and setup
schedule.exercise: Write a reusable function library plan listing the numerical routines you will build this course and their input and output conventions.

tasks.title: Compute the relative error propagated through four arithmetic expressions with given input uncertainties and check against interval bounds
Plot the Taylor polynomials of sin(x) of order 1, 3, 5 and 7 against the true function and tabulate the error at x equals 1
Write a tested numerical routines module with a convergence-checking helper and a function that estimates the observed order of convergence

schedule.title: Root finding I: bisection, fixed point and Newton
schedule.exercise: Show by hand two steps of Newton's method for x squared minus 2 and compare with the true root.

tasks.title: Apply bisection to find the root of cos(x) minus x on an interval, tabulate the error against the bound and confirm the iteration count
Test three rearrangements of the same equation as fixed-point iterations and use the contraction condition to explain which converge
Implement Newton's method, show quadratic convergence on a simple root and linear convergence on a double root, and fix the slow case

schedule.title: Root finding II: secant, polynomials and applications
schedule.exercise: Write a half-page comparison of bisection, Newton and secant for use inside a financial spreadsheet, covering robustness and speed.

tasks.title: Implement the secant method and false position, and compare their iteration counts on one equation to a tolerance of 1e-8
Evaluate a degree-6 polynomial using Horner's scheme, find its roots with deflation and compare the work with naive evaluation
Find the interest rate that equates the present value of a loan repayment schedule to its principal, using a hybrid method that never diverges

schedule.title: Direct methods for linear systems
schedule.exercise: Perform Gaussian elimination by hand on a 3 by 3 system with small pivot and show why pivoting changes the answer.

tasks.title: Solve a 3 by 3 system by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting, listing the row operations and checking the residual
Compute the LU factorisation of a 4 by 4 matrix and use it to solve three right-hand sides, comparing flops with repeated elimination
Solve Hilbert systems of size 4 to 12, compute their condition numbers and show how the error grows far beyond the residual

schedule.title: Banded systems and least squares
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph why tridiagonal systems from a heat equation are solved in linear time rather than cubic.

tasks.title: Solve a 6 by 6 tridiagonal system with the Thomas algorithm and compare the result and the operation count with full elimination
Fit a straight line to 10 noisy points by normal equations and by QR, and compare the coefficients and residual norms
Fit a degree-8 polynomial with normal equations and with QR, show the loss of accuracy through the condition number, and explain which to prefer

schedule.title: Iterative methods and eigenvalues
schedule.exercise: Compute by hand two Jacobi iterations for a diagonally dominant 3 by 3 system and compare with the exact solution.

tasks.title: Run Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel on a diagonally dominant 4 by 4 system, plot the error for 20 iterations and compare the rates
Find the dominant eigenvalue of a 4 by 4 matrix with the power method, then the smallest with the inverse power method, and compare with a library result
Compute PageRank for a graph of six web pages using the power method with damping, and show how the ranking changes with the damping factor

schedule.title: Interpolation
schedule.exercise: Sketch by hand why interpolating a bell-shaped curve with equally spaced points at high degree oscillates near the ends.

tasks.title: Build the Lagrange and Newton interpolating polynomials through five points and show they give the same curve and the same error at a test point
Interpolate Runge's function with 11 equally spaced nodes and with Chebyshev nodes, plot both and compare the maximum errors
Construct natural and clamped cubic splines through 8 measured points, check continuity of the second derivative and compare their end behaviour

schedule.title: Curve fitting and approximation
schedule.exercise: Decide which model suits a rainfall record, linear, polynomial or exponential, and justify your choice with a plot and a residual sketch.

tasks.title: Fit a line and a quadratic to 12 data points, plot both and compute the sum of squared residuals to pick the better fit
Draw a Bezier curve through four control points, split it with de Casteljau's algorithm and verify the curve passes through its end points
Fit exponential and polynomial models to monthly sales data, hold out the last three months, and judge which model forecasts better

schedule.title: Numerical differentiation and integration
schedule.exercise: Compute by hand the trapezoidal and Simpson's rule approximations for an integral over four intervals and compare the errors.

tasks.title: Estimate the derivative of sin(x) at 1 with forward, backward and central differences for step sizes from 0.1 down to 1e-12, and plot the error
Compare the composite trapezoidal and Simpson's rules for an integral at 4, 8 and 16 intervals and check the observed error ratios against theory
Implement Romberg integration and an adaptive Simpson routine, and compare the number of function evaluations needed to reach a given tolerance

schedule.title: Gaussian quadrature and applications
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph when a Gaussian rule with few points beats a composite rule with many points.

tasks.title: Apply 2, 3 and 5-point Gauss-Legendre rules to an integral and compare the errors with Simpson's rule at the same cost
Integrate a measured river discharge curve of 24 hourly readings to find total volume, and estimate the uncertainty from the reading error
Compute probabilities from a probability density function that has no closed form integral using adaptive quadrature, and verify that the total probability is one

schedule.title: Initial value problems for ODEs
schedule.exercise: Calculate three steps of Euler's method for y prime equals y with y(0) equal 1 and compare each with the exact value.

tasks.title: Solve y prime equals y with Euler's method at step sizes 0.2, 0.1 and 0.05, then show the global error halves as the step is halved
Implement RK4 and compare its accuracy and cost with Euler on a test problem, then add an adaptive step size controller
Implement a fourth-order Adams-Bashforth predictor with an Adams-Moulton corrector, start it with RK4, and compare against RK4 for the same accuracy

schedule.title: Systems, stiffness and project
schedule.exercise: Write the project plan for simulating an epidemic, listing the model, parameters, methods and tests you will use to validate it.

tasks.title: Convert a second-order pendulum equation into a first-order system and solve it with RK4, checking that energy is conserved over 10 periods
Solve a stiff test equation with explicit Euler and implicit Euler at several step sizes, plot stability and explain which steps are stable
Simulate an SIR epidemic with RK4, validate it against a limit case and the final size relation, and write a short interpretation for a health officer
